8858e40168334238:2792.summary: Researchers designed and formally verified a blockchain-based electronic invoice system on Ethereum to solve duplicate reimbursement, authenticity, and single-point-of-failure issues in centralized architectures. The system models invoices as non-fungible, non-tradable tokens transitioning through guarded states to guarantee reimbursement uniqueness, face integrity, and authorization soundness. Implemented as a Solidity contract, the architecture also serves as a secure safety envelope for LLM-based reimbursement agents, provably preventing duplicate or forged claims even when agent internal policies fail.
8858e40168334238:2792.one_liner: Ethereum-based verified e-invoice systems prevent duplicate reimbursements and act as security envelopes for autonomous LLM finance agents.
8858e40168334238:2792.bottom_line: Smart contract invariants can mathematically prevent duplicate and fraudulent invoice reimbursements while serving as an unbreakable safety envelope for LLM agents.

claims.text: The core invariants are machine-checked using Solidity SMTChecker, proving inductive validity across all reachable transaction sequences.
claims.support_span: The core invariants are machine-checked using Solidity SMTChecker, proving inductive validity across all reachable transaction sequences.

21160fe603076369:2613.summary: Provenance-based intrusion detection systems often produce false positives and hard-to-interpret outputs when analyzed by LLMs. To address this, researchers introduced ANCHOR, a context-grounded and stateful provenance investigation framework. ANCHOR combines anomaly calibration, evidence curation, and a confidence-gated Attack-Tracking Cache to correlate evidence across windows and reconstruct kill-chain attack narratives. Evaluations across multiple DARPA Transparent Computing datasets show improved indicator-of-compromise recovery and attack attribution.
21160fe603076369:2613.one_liner: ANCHOR provides stateful, context-grounded LLM investigation over system provenance graphs to accurately reconstruct attack narratives.
21160fe603076369:2613.bottom_line: Combining deployment context with a confidence-gated attack tracking cache allows LLMs to accurately convert system audit logs into coherent attack narratives.

claims.text: We present ANCHOR, an investigation-oriented provenance system that combines evidence curation with context-grounded LLM reasoning.
claims.support_span: We present ANCHOR, an investigation-oriented provenance system that combines evidence curation with context-grounded LLM reasoning.

key_facts: Datasets evaluated: Six DARPA Transparent Computing E3/E5 datasets across three operating systems

1651c8818f70bf2b:2763.summary: Zero-knowledge proofs are vital for verifying private LLM inference and training data usage, but understanding zero-knowledge-friendly quantization remains limited due to arithmetic and constraint costs. Researchers conducted a systematic study across nine language models, evaluating weight, activation, and nonlinear lookup precisions. The findings reveal that activation precision is far more sensitive than weight precision, and RMSNorm inverse-square-root lookups create major performance bottlenecks that require selective precision increases.
1651c8818f70bf2b:2763.one_liner: Systematic evaluation of ZK-friendly quantization shows that activations and RMSNorm lookups dictate the proving costs and utility of ZK-LLMs.
1651c8818f70bf2b:2763.bottom_line: Conventional low-bit quantization heuristics fail in ZK-LLM inference, making operator-aware precision selection essential for balancing proof costs and model utility.

claims.text: Our results show that activation precision is substantially more sensitive than weight precision, while nonlinear lookup approximations can become the dominant source of utility degradation.
claims.support_span: Our results show that activation precision is substantially more sensitive than weight precision, while nonlinear lookup approximations can become the dominant source of utility degradation.

key_facts: Models evaluated: Nine language models including Qwen2.5-14B and Qwen3-30B-A3B

37eecf2f8ea11fb7:2452.summary: Detecting major depressive disorder involves heterogeneous multimodal data such as interview recordings and sensor measurements, which require customized prediction pipelines. Existing approaches struggle to autonomously revise pipelines based on experimental feedback. To overcome this, researchers proposed MERID, a framework using experience-based recursive self-improvement, grounded state construction, coupled pipeline exploration, and evidence-guided evolution to build and verify classification pipelines.
37eecf2f8ea11fb7:2452.one_liner: MERID applies recursive self-improvement agents to autonomously build and refine multimodal pipelines for major depression analysis.
37eecf2f8ea11fb7:2452.bottom_line: Autonomous agent frameworks utilizing experience-based recursive self-improvement can successfully optimize complex multimodal pipelines for clinical medical analysis.

claims.text: To this end, we propose Multimodal Exploration via Recursive Self-Improvement Agents for Major Depression Analysis (MERID).
claims.support_span: To this end, we propose Multimodal Exploration via Recursive Self-Improvement Agents for Major Depression Analysis (MERID).

63d6d7dd6a0ced20:2225.summary: Researchers investigated where large language models decide to comply with prompt injection attacks using layer-by-layer causal activation patching across five models ranging from 4B to 32B parameters. The study discovered a clear dissociation: while attack information is present in the first layer, causal leverage over behavior is negligible until a late-layer bottleneck in the final third of the network. Patching this specific bottleneck reverses compliance in 77 to 92 percent of cases, revealing a compact linear subspace responsible for rule-breaking decisions.
63d6d7dd6a0ced20:2225.one_liner: LLMs decide to comply with prompt injections at a specific late-layer network bottleneck rather than early layers.
63d6d7dd6a0ced20:2225.bottom_line: Prompt injection compliance is controlled by a compact linear subspace located exclusively in the final third of an LLM's network layers.

claims.text: Patching this bottleneck reverses compliance in 77--92\% of cases.
claims.support_span: Patching this bottleneck reverses compliance in 77--92\% of cases.

ae8a6109ed675322:2384.summary: Many existing machine learning-based network intrusion detection systems suffer from inflated performance metrics due to labeling errors, inconsistent flow extraction, and data leakage. To fix this, researchers presented a comprehensive benchmark pipeline using corrected PCAP-level labeling and evaluated eleven tabular classifiers across binary, nine-class, and fifteen-class granularities. A soft-voting ensemble achieved top-tier macro-F1 scores across all levels, offering a reproducible reference point for future IDS research.
ae8a6109ed675322:2384.one_liner: A rigorously corrected network intrusion detection benchmark pipeline provides reliable, reproducible evaluation metrics for ML classifiers.
ae8a6109ed675322:2384.bottom_line: Correcting pipeline flaws and PCAP labels in network intrusion detection datasets establishes reliable performance baselines for machine learning classifiers.

claims.text: A soft-voting ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM obtains the best fine-tier macro-F1 of 0.955, with coarse and binary macro-F1 scores of 0.980 and 0.999, respectively.
claims.support_span: A soft-voting ensemble of Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM obtains the best fine-tier macro-F1 of 0.955, with coarse and binary macro-F1 scores of 0.980 and 0.999, respectively.

dcaf8f9d323af538:1624.summary: Temporal abstraction via options helps reinforcement learning agents explore large environments, but traditional state-reaching approaches target all state aspects simultaneously, causing an explosion of narrow options. Researchers introduced an algorithm that identifies a small, relevant subset of features for each subgoal instead, yielding options that generalize broadly. This method achieves rapid exploration in sparse-reward, image-based domains including Montezuma's Revenge.
dcaf8f9d323af538:1624.one_liner: Feature-based option discovery improves exploration efficiency in complex reinforcement learning environments without state-space explosions.
dcaf8f9d323af538:1624.bottom_line: Targeting specific feature subsets instead of entire states prevents option-space explosion and accelerates reinforcement learning exploration.

claims.text: Our approach learns abstract, transferrable options and achieves rapid exploration in three sparse-reward, image-based domains, including the Atari game MontezumasRevenge.
claims.support_span: Our approach learns abstract, transferrable options and achieves rapid exploration in three sparse-reward, image-based domains, including the Atari game MontezumasRevenge.

key_facts: Test environments: Three sparse-reward, image-based domains including Montezuma's Revenge

96cfffe591c3e51e:2502.summary: Semantic watermarking embeds detectable signals into LLM-generated text to resist removal attacks, but often suffers from semantic narrowing due to poor alignment with natural generation preferences. To solve this, researchers introduced HammingMark, which uses semantic hashes of preceding sentences to accept candidate tokens falling within a dynamic Hamming neighborhood. Experiments on C4 and BookSum datasets show that HammingMark achieves strong robustness and high detectability while requiring only 2.2 sampled candidates per sentence—a 72.8 percent reduction over existing methods.
96cfffe591c3e51e:2502.one_liner: HammingMark improves LLM watermarking efficiency and quality by validating tokens within Hamming neighborhoods in compact hash space.
96cfffe591c3e51e:2502.bottom_line: Hamming-neighborhood semantic hashing eliminates semantic narrowing in LLM watermarks while cutting resampling overhead by nearly 73 percent.

claims.text: Experiments on C4 and BookSum show that HammingMark achieves strong robustness, high detectability, and near-unwatermarked generation quality, requiring only 2.2 sampled candidates per sentence,a 72.8% reduction compared with the most sampling-efficient existing method.
claims.support_span: Experiments on C4 and BookSum show that HammingMark achieves strong robustness, high detectability, and near-unwatermarked generation quality, requiring only 2.2 sampled candidates per sentence,a 72.8% reduction compared with the most sampling-efficient existing method.

90c3f51b6a3eb310:1766.summary: While large language models show strong potential for lossless data compression, autoregressive decoding imposes high computational costs and low throughput. Researchers proposed HyperZip, a framework leveraging diffusion-based LLMs with multi-token prediction to accelerate data compression. HyperZip employs a hypernetwork to generate data-specific updates from context representations without requiring costly fine-tuning, achieving a superior trade-off between compression rate and decoding speed.
90c3f51b6a3eb310:1766.one_liner: HyperZip accelerates LLM-based data compression using diffusion models and hypernetworks without requiring expensive fine-tuning.
90c3f51b6a3eb310:1766.bottom_line: Diffusion-based LLMs paired with hypernetworks overcome the throughput bottlenecks of autoregressive lossless data compression.

claims.text: We propose HyperZip, an efficient and scalable LLM-based compression framework that leverages diffusion-based LLMs (dLLMs) with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) to accelerate LLM-based data compression processes.
claims.support_span: We propose HyperZip, an efficient and scalable LLM-based compression framework that leverages diffusion-based LLMs (dLLMs) with Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) to accelerate LLM-based data compression processes.

40ffa32490b8f34a:2657.summary: Adversarial machine learning has largely focused on integrity, but availability threats such as latency and energy-latency attacks are increasingly consequential. These attacks increase inference work, response time, or resource consumption, causing deadline misses and throughput collapse in autonomous driving, interactive services, and tool-using LLM agents. Researchers surveyed this cross-domain literature by classifying attacks based on intermediate-work amplification and computational bottlenecks, providing a unified threat-model taxonomy and defense abstractions.
40ffa32490b8f34a:2657.one_liner: A comprehensive survey of deep learning latency attacks unifies availability threats across autonomous systems and LLMs.
40ffa32490b8f34a:2657.bottom_line: Intermediate-work amplification attacks can trigger system-wide availability failures across deep learning pipelines unless bounded by work-budget defense abstractions.

claims.text: Many attacks share one mechanism, intermediate-work amplification, motivating a work-budget defense abstraction; we distinguish caps on the work entering an expensive stage from caps on the results leaving it.
claims.support_span: Many attacks share one mechanism, intermediate-work amplification, motivating a work-budget defense abstraction; we distinguish caps on the work entering an expensive stage from caps on the results leaving it.

bcb2f5530035f978:2638.summary: Running coding agents over long horizons is difficult because context windows grow with every observation and text-based history maintenance fails to track code dependencies accurately. To solve this, researchers proposed StateTape, a framework that models code repositories as symbol-level code graphs to track changes as the code edits. StateTape marks which symbols are affected by writes, using a small manager model to clear falsified history records and retrieve needed context, thereby increasing agent resolve rates across benchmarks.
bcb2f5530035f978:2638.one_liner: StateTape maintains precise coding agent context during long-horizon tasks by modeling repositories as symbol-level code graphs rather than plain text.
bcb2f5530035f978:2638.bottom_line: Tracking symbol-level code dependencies instead of raw text history prevents coding agents from relying on falsified context during long tasks.

claims.text: Empirically, we demonstrate that StateTape can effectively clear falsified records and retrieve what is needed, and thus achieve a higher resolve rate in all experiments spanned by six coding agents and three edit-heavy benchmarks with little computational overhead.
claims.support_span: Empirically, we demonstrate that StateTape can effectively clear falsified records and retrieve what is needed, and thus achieve a higher resolve rate in all experiments spanned by six coding agents and three edit-heavy benchmarks with little computational overhead.

36b494a2eee7a243:2362.summary: This study evaluates whether automated generation of LLM harnesses provides useful task specialization or simply benefits from repeated execution. Testing eight generated harnesses alongside a baseline with nine byte-identical copies across 386 MATH-500 tasks, the authors found that identical programs yield 2.16 percentage points of repeat-averaged oracle headroom. While generated programs show repeatable score patterns, these largely reflect persistent weaknesses rather than genuine specialization. The findings demonstrate that coverage and repeatability alone cannot justify claims of useful harness diversity.
36b494a2eee7a243:2362.one_liner: Evaluating LLM harness specialization requires proving task advantages persist across executions rather than merely repeating identical programs.
36b494a2eee7a243:2362.bottom_line: Repeated execution of identical LLM programs can mimic task specialization gains, proving that coverage metrics alone are insufficient to validate harness diversity.

claims.text: Identical programs yield 2.16 percentage points of repeat-averaged oracle headroom.
claims.support_span: Identical programs yield 2.16 percentage points of repeat-averaged oracle headroom.

key_facts: Oracle headroom: 2.16 percentage points from identical programs

7dfd8d6dd8f3d3c9:2263.summary: Cell Painting-based mechanism of action prediction is typically handled through representation matching, which often suffers from noisy retrieved neighbors due to batch effects and cytotoxicity. To address this, researchers propose PhenoAIR, a reliability-aware multi-agent framework that treats retrieved neighbors as uncertain observations requiring controller-guided refinement and calibration. PhenoAIR uses offline reference-set calibration to weight evidence by source reliability, phenotype stability, and mechanism-level confusion. Evaluated on a JUMP Cell Painting benchmark, PhenoAIR outperforms standard representation-matching and LLM-based baselines across open-world settings.
7dfd8d6dd8f3d3c9:2263.one_liner: PhenoAIR improves biological mechanism prediction from Cell Painting profiles by treating retrieved morphological neighbors as uncertain evidence requiring multi-agent reasoning.

5f7bbdcf07f1516c:2411.summary: Semantic caches in LLM serving are vulnerable to poisoning attacks because retrieval relies solely on embedding similarity rather than answer validity. Attackers can exploit this by pairing a rewrite of a target query with a residual content string that elicits a malicious response while maintaining high cosine similarity. To counter this, researchers propose a defense leveraging Deletion Gain and an Answer Check to identify and remove malicious residual text from cache keys. Across three attack classes, this defense blocks 82.0% to 98.2% of poisoned entries at a 5% false-positive rate with negligible overhead.
5f7bbdcf07f1516c:2411.one_liner: Defend LLM semantic caches against poisoning by using Deletion Gain to strip malicious residual text while preserving semantic match validity.
5f7bbdcf07f1516c:2411.bottom_line: Semantic cache poisoning can be effectively mitigated by analyzing query structure for rewrite-residuals rather than trusting embedding similarity alone.

27c57d7afd22a61a:2049.summary: Agentic retrieval-augmented generation systems are susceptible to retriever backdoors where an attacker supplies a compromised retriever checkpoint without needing corpus write access. This allows adversaries to suppress evidence, persistently retrieve specific documents, or inflate latency costs by steering the agent into prolonged searches. To hide these behaviors, attackers can use a controlled inject-and-remove cycle that unlearns a weaker backdoor to fool detectors with an illusion of purification. These findings show that weak defense mechanisms can inadvertently be leveraged by attackers to conceal backdoored retrievers.
27c57d7afd22a61a:2049.one_liner: Attackers can conceal backdoored RAG retrievers by exploiting weak defense mechanisms using an inject-and-remove unlearning cycle.
27c57d7afd22a61a:2049.bottom_line: Purification defenses in agentic RAG can be subverted by attackers to conceal malicious retriever checkpoints while maintaining functional backdoors.

f704ebf85950534b:1838.summary: Power system operation benchmarks for reinforcement learning are traditionally bottlenecked by narrow scopes and CPU-based simulation workflows. To resolve this, researchers introduced PowerZooJax, a JAX-based benchmark suite for power system reinforcement learning tasks. By rewriting power flow, economic dispatch, market clearing, and device dynamics as JAX computation graphs, the framework keeps the entire training and evaluation loop entirely on the GPU. Experiments demonstrate major speedups over CPU-based alternatives alongside standardized evaluations for policy returns, safety violations, and stress conditions.

f704ebf85950534b:1838.bottom_line: Moving power system simulation workflows to GPU-based JAX computation graphs eliminates CPU bottlenecks for reinforcement learning benchmarks.

f39577ed0bb74ad0:2291.summary: Graph-based approximate nearest neighbor search indices are typically constructed using embedding geometry rather than semantic relevance to queries, resulting in a geometry-semantic mismatch. To resolve this without relying solely on query-time reranking, researchers propose LLM-Guided Graph Pruning, a framework that leverages LLM reasoning to refine the underlying ANN graph index itself. The method identifies structurally low-value neighbors and replaces them with LLM-selected alternatives while preserving sparsity and efficient navigability. Experiments show that this approach consistently improves end-to-end retrieval performance over standard greedy search and query-time reranking.
f39577ed0bb74ad0:2291.one_liner: LLM-Guided Graph Pruning directly resolves the geometry-semantic mismatch in vector indices by using LLMs to restructure graph neighbors.
f39577ed0bb74ad0:2291.bottom_line: Refining vector index graph topology directly via LLM guidance improves retrieval performance beyond what query-time reranking can achieve.

The system generates coordinated narrations, grounds them in visual evidence, and applies visual actions to guide user attention. Using a hierarchical search strategy, FigAct reduces token usage by approximately 40 times while improving explanation clarity.

270c3b97a266ac13:2062.bottom_line: Active visual manipulation of scientific figures by multimodal models provides clearer explanations and significantly reduces token consumption compared to pure text translation.

89355b5ad1291336:2771.summary: Researchers have introduced A2A-TIBA, an attack method combining indirect prompt injection with bypass circumvention in multi-agent systems using protocols like ACP and A2A. To better evaluate defenses, the authors developed GDA Measurement, a red-team testbed using raw context capture via an LLM gateway, and proposed the ELA-ITL three-layer isomorphic attack-defense model separating defenses into envelope packaging, LLM recognition, and agent interception. a21d05cf6500c8af:2669.summary: Researchers investigating the use of small language models (SLMs) in agent harnesses around frontier LLM planners evaluated Qwen3 (0.6B to 8B models) across four microtasks with strict confidence-interval eligibility thresholds. 5e1f1974e4f12a7b:2715.summary: Researchers proposed a pipeline to automatically generate ontology-grounded multiple-choice question benchmarks from OWL 2 ontologies to evaluate logical reasoning in scientific AI models. Correct answers are grounded by design, while incorrect distractors are generated by perturbing class definition axioms and verified by an OWL reasoner. The pipeline was tested on Pizza, PMDco, and DOID ontologies, generating 112, 2,491, and 15,216 MCQs respectively. 90b9d6dce6eb5b63:3697.summary: A high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-92142, has been discovered in Apache Karaf where JMX MBeanServer lifecycle operations like createMBean, registerMBean, and unregisterMBean are omitted from the KarafMBeanServerGuard. 4eeb8815d103269f:902.summary: A critical privilege escalation and remote code execution vulnerability, CVE-2026-91048, has been identified in Apache Karaf due to missing command scope ACL configuration files. Because Karaf's command guard defaults to allowing commands with no matching ACL rules, authenticated shell users with only viewer-level access can run all commands within the jdbc and jms scopes. Exploiting this, an attacker can use jdbc:ds-create to inject an unvalidated JDBC URL into a pax-jdbc-config factory Configuration, leveraging connection-time parameters like H2 INIT=RUNSCRIPT to achieve arbitrary code execution. This bypasses the administrative restrictions protecting commands like shell:exec, resulting in a CVSS base score of 9.8.

4eeb8815d103269f:902.bottom_line: An unprivileged shell user in Apache Karaf can achieve remote code execution via unvalidated JDBC connection parameters due to missing default ACL configurations.

f62625896671a776:2197.summary: Researchers have introduced APEX, a method that constructs adversarial skill chains to hijack LLM agents by exploiting multi-step workflows. 39c6dea226cc4bf5:2566.summary: A new survey explores the safety challenges of self-evolving AI agents that update their own parameters, memories, and tool definitions post-deployment. The researchers introduce the SAVER framework to track how reusable experiences can lead to safety violations when adapted or reused in new contexts. 66ef9f74187a686a:1957.summary: A systematic analysis of LLM-generated preference distributions reveals that while models are self-coherent, there is significant discordance between different model families and scales. 66ef9f74187a686a:1957.bottom_line: Do not rely on LLMs as standardized proxies for human preferences, as results are highly sensitive to the specific model architecture rather than the prompt.

claims.text: At the same time, we observe substantial discordance across both model families and scales, with little consensus even among their most probable outcomes.

claims.text: Our findings indicate that outcomes are influenced more by the choice of model than by the wording of the prompt, challenging the common assumption that sufficiently capable LLMs produce similar preference distributions when used as stand-ins for survey respondents.

2af83112f95570a7:2649.summary: Researchers investigated whether frozen, zero-shot large language models can provide retraining-free control in hierarchical cyber defense across networks of varying scales. Specifically, a frozen 70B model held successful lateral movement to about 1% of steps and attacker impact near zero across small, medium, and large networks without retraining.
2af83112f95570a7:2649.one_liner: Frozen 70B LLMs can act as effective tactical execution agents in hierarchical cyber defense, maintaining strong security performance across varying network scales without retraining.

06613c4c858abb9e:2646.one_liner: LLM safety routing evaluations suffer from severe bias under distribution shift, and routing benefits shrink dramatically when scored honestly.
06613c4c858abb9e:2646.bottom_line: Standard LLM safety routing benchmarks provide misleadingly high performance estimates because their comparator selection breaks under distribution shift.

13713bf66ce09fa8:1987.summary: Researchers proposed MemFit, a long-term memory system for conversational agents that aims to reduce the cost and latency of memory operations. Unlike systems that rely on expensive LLM calls for construction or compress data by discarding surface details, MemFit stores each turn verbatim in an append-only store with LLM-free insertion. It uses an LLM-free multi-path retrieval strategy combining lexical and semantic signals with cross-encoder reranking. Empirical results on LoCoMo, MemGallery, and LongMemEval-S show that MemFit achieves state-of-the-art performance while reducing memory construction time and cost.

5f03340a3c340315:2738.summary: Researchers introduced RISED, a framework using rubrics for agentic multi-environment selection and self-distillation to train generalist LLM agents across diverse interactive environments. Instead of relying solely on scalar rewards, RISED uses an LLM judge to tag rollouts with a predefined rubric vocabulary to guide online data selection and policy supervision. Positive rubrics provide context for an on-policy self-distillation teacher, while negative rubrics steer generation away from recurring failure modes. Across backbones, RISED achieved the highest mean pass rate across evaluated environments.
5f03340a3c340315:2738.one_liner: RISED improves multi-environment LLM agent training by using rubric-based textual feedback for online data selection and self-distillation.
5f03340a3c340315:2738.bottom_line: Using rubric-based textual feedback instead of scalar rewards alone allows LLM agents to generalize better across diverse interactive environments.

claims.support_span: Across model backbones, RISED achieves the highest mean pass rate across environments and ranks first or second in every individual environment.

ef5ece8fb88b20d8:2597.summary: Researchers introduced ActiveSaddler, an automated curriculum learning method for optimizing LLM agent harnesses by treating the training curriculum as a non-stationary bandit. As prompts, tool interfaces, and control logic evolve, ActiveSaddler abstracts recurring failures into reusable failure-pattern arms and dynamically balances revisiting weaknesses with exploring unseen scenarios. Experiments on GAIA2 and Terminal-Bench 2.0 showed that ActiveSaddler improved test Pass@1 by 4.4 and 7.5 percentage points, respectively, compared to a fixed scenario order.
ef5ece8fb88b20d8:2597.one_liner: ActiveSaddler co-evolves training curricula with LLM agent harnesses, boosting performance by dynamically targeting emerging failure patterns.
ef5ece8fb88b20d8:2597.bottom_line: Automated curriculum learning that dynamically adapts training scenarios alongside agent harness updates significantly improves agent optimization outcomes.

1d9ebfbb76c99688:2205.summary: Researchers analyzed the shape of memory use in long-horizon language agents and discovered that under repeated retrieval, agent memory concentrates on a small core while leaving rare states in a heavy-tailed distribution. Motivated by this finding, they proposed the Core-Tail World Model (CTWM), a rank-based memory controller that allocates prompt budgets using a single exponent while retaining a summarized tail. CTWM reduces prompt token usage across benchmark environments while maintaining state coverage and task accuracy.
1d9ebfbb76c99688:2205.one_liner: CTWM leverages heavy-tailed memory traces to optimize prompt token budgets and reduce prediction error in long-horizon language agents.
1d9ebfbb76c99688:2205.bottom_line: Agent memory naturally exhibits heavy-tailed traces under finite context, which can be exploited using rank-based controllers to achieve token efficiency without accuracy loss.

claims.text: On Synthetic Graph World, CTWM preserves full state and transition coverage, reduces prompt tokens by 5.9%, and lowers bottom-half tail prediction error by 13.6% relative to a graph-memory baseline.
claims.support_span: On Synthetic Graph World, CTWM preserves full state and transition coverage, reduces prompt tokens by 5.9%, and lowers bottom-half tail prediction error by 13.6% relative to a graph-memory baseline.

a3a0eec377ea25db:2250.summary: Researchers presented Kepler, an open-source harness for evaluating agents on ARC-AGI-3 that represents hypotheses as executable world models and validates them through retrospective transition checks and conditional prediction checks. a3a0eec377ea25db:2250.bottom_line: Auditable world models can solve interactive agent benchmarks like ARC-AGI-3, but public-set scores alone offer limited discriminative value due to hidden evaluation vulnerabilities.

7313d5e64734621e:2746.summary: Self-modifying AI agents that replace, fork, or roll back identity-bearing software risk breaking permission boundaries across generations. Researchers defined authorization succession to conserve authority across a single-parent generation forest using cryptographic manifests, invariants, and staged reservations. An evaluation across 32 registered decisions and external adapters demonstrated that the protocol successfully enforces population-safe succession and rejects semantic mutants.
7313d5e64734621e:2746.one_liner: Authorization succession protocols can secure self-modifying AI agent populations by binding authority across replacements, forks, and rollbacks.
7313d5e64734621e:2746.bottom_line: Managing authorization across self-modifying AI agent populations requires strict lineage binding and staged reservations to prevent unauthorized privilege accumulation.

f096ef7fd0ed3668:2747.summary: Computer-use agents (CUAs) use persistent workspace memory files that mix user instructions and external claims at the same privilege level, enabling persistent memory attacks where benign external content injects malicious instructions into memory. To mitigate this, researchers proposed ZoneClaw, which establishes memory-zoning with hierarchical trust zones and asymmetric privilege roles. External claims persist in a low-trust zone and must cross an explicit authority boundary to guide actions. Across evaluations, ZoneClaw drastically reduced attack success rates while preserving agent utility.
f096ef7fd0ed3668:2747.one_liner: ZoneClaw mitigates persistent memory injection attacks in computer-use agents by separating low-trust workspace memory from high-trust execution authority.
f096ef7fd0ed3668:2747.bottom_line: Persistent memory attacks in computer-use agents can be effectively mitigated by enforcing strict memory-zoning and authority boundaries between ingested content and actionable execution.

a5ec8ba43286576e:2715.summary: To address privacy risks and PII leakage in LLMs deployed in sensitive domains, researchers introduced Locket (LoRA-Oriented Control via Keyed Entry Tokens). Locket trains fine-grained LoRA adapters representing different access policies, paired with a gating module that associates a keyed entry token with a specific adapter via hard routing. A valid token unlocks private knowledge, while a missing or invalid token triggers a privacy-preserving adapter that redacts sensitive content. Evaluations across models like Qwen3, Llama-3.2, and Gemma-2 showed that Locket maintains utility when tokens are valid and substantially reduces PII leakage when tokens are absent.
a5ec8ba43286576e:2715.one_liner: Locket provides fine-grained, token-gated access control for LLMs using LoRA adapters to prevent PII leakage without sacrificing utility.
a5ec8ba43286576e:2715.bottom_line: Tokenized key-gated LoRA adapter routing allows enterprises to enforce strict access control over private data inside LLMs without retraining base models.

claims.text: Our extensive experiments demonstrate that, when the correct token is provided, Locket preserves perplexity comparable to fine-tuning on raw data (without any defense).
claims.support_span: Our extensive experiments demonstrate that, when the correct token is provided, Locket preserves perplexity comparable to fine-tuning on raw data (without any defense).

3760b79ae828ac9b:2540.summary: Tool-using agents can output citations and execution logs that remain structurally valid while being mismatched or transplanted across claims, actions, or source versions. To address this, researchers introduced a claim-anchored execution contract that jointly binds emitted claims, exact source spans, ordered execution prefixes, and source access states into cryptographic receipts. A deterministic verifier reconstructs these bindings before semantic evaluation. Across 1,280 cross-object attacks, the joint contract detected 99.61% of substitutions.
3760b79ae828ac9b:2540.one_liner: Claim-anchored execution contracts prevent citation and evidence tampering in tool-using agents by cryptographically binding claims to their execution traces and source spans.
3760b79ae828ac9b:2540.bottom_line: Auditing tool-using agents requires jointly binding claims, source evidence, and execution traces to prevent citation-transplantation attacks.

b044d2469ff235f4:2638.summary: Researchers introduced Praxa, an agent harness designed to make the states of an LLM agent—ranging from action proposals and authority checks to external read-backs and reviewed promotions—explicit through deterministic admission and brokered execution. Evaluation results across internal unit tests, Terminal-Bench pilots, and coordination-proxy comparisons demonstrated that while Praxa establishes an evidence-bound architecture for authority-to-effect transitions, current data does not establish improved quality, adversarial security, or production safety lift.
b044d2469ff235f4:2638.one_liner: Praxa provides an evidence-bound harness architecture for governed AI agent execution, making authority-to-effect transitions explicit and testable.
b044d2469ff235f4:2638.bottom_line: Governing AI agent execution requires architectural separation between action proposals, authority checks, and verified external effects.

67ac19568dcc6aa1:2730.summary: Agent developers frequently evaluate prompts, tools, and debuggers using simulator-grounded verifiers. However, if verifier probes or predicates encode target identities, an optimizer can appear effective without resolving genuine ambiguity—essentially because the verifier leaked the answer. The authors discovered this failure mode in a closed-loop agent debugger and replaced solver-first evaluation with a support-gated verification contract that verifies evidence eligibility and non-revelation before component optimization.
67ac19568dcc6aa1:2730.one_liner: Verifiers in agent debugging can accidentally leak answers and invalidate solver evaluations unless evidence eligibility is strictly gated.
67ac19568dcc6aa1:2730.bottom_line: Agent optimization benchmarks are flawed if the underlying verifier leaks target identities, necessitating support-gated verification contracts before running solvers.

1df3ee805a6bd359:1740.summary: Researchers introduced EviGraph for proof-carrying selective recommendation over temporal public-service knowledge graphs. Public-service recommendations require strict evidence matching service scope and dates, but treating every missing detail as decisive can cause unnecessary abstention. EviGraph distinguishes critical decision requirements from non-essential information using a language agent linked to a temporal knowledge graph, with a deterministic checker verifying support. Evaluation on a Hong Kong public-service benchmark showed that this approach reduces unnecessary abstention.
1df3ee805a6bd359:1740.one_liner: EviGraph uses a language agent and temporal knowledge graphs to reduce unnecessary abstention in evidence-based public-service recommendations.
1df3ee805a6bd359:1740.bottom_line: Reliable evidence-based recommendations require explicitly defining critical decision requirements rather than applying rigid verification to every missing detail.

80892eda7e1f5aab:2586.summary: Researchers formulated grounded correction arbitration for text-based embodied agents to determine how an agent should respond when a user's correction might be incorrect. They implemented GAVA, which uses observation-bounded evidence, legal probes, and a one-step expected-loss rule to choose among accepting, rejecting, inspecting the world, or asking the speaker. Evaluations in text-based ALFWorld showed high correction accuracy, though results did not establish a general advantage of environmental value of information over clarification.
80892eda7e1f5aab:2586.one_liner: GAVA provides a principled arbitration framework for text-based embodied agents to evaluate potentially incorrect user corrections using observation bounds.
80892eda7e1f5aab:2586.bottom_line: Embodied agents can reliably arbitrate conflicting user corrections by combining observation-bounded evidence with expected-loss decision rules.

f7cf8f6241f5d2db:2035.summary: Multi-agent systems often face a safety dilemma where benign individual contributions jointly enable prohibited actions, but blocking all sensitive actions hinders collaboration. f7cf8f6241f5d2db:2035.bottom_line: Multi-agent systems can safely collaborate without excessive blocking if authorization and object identity are strictly paired with verifiable execution components.

68db07d2bbf4fcc7:1910.summary: Large Language Models can be implanted with backdoors during training that trigger unwanted behavior, while existing defenses often inadvertently degrade model performance on benign prompts. To resolve this, researchers propose NEEDLE, a training-free method for targeted backdoor removal using activation vectors to estimate backdoor directions and refusal subspaces. By applying sequential weight orthogonalisation, NEEDLE suppresses the backdoor without requiring a clean reference model or original poisoned data. Evaluations across multiple model families show that NEEDLE achieves a 0% attack success rate on challenging code injection attacks while maintaining minimal KL divergence and preserving model capabilities.

68db07d2bbf4fcc7:1910.bottom_line: Targeted LLM backdoors can be completely neutralized via weight orthogonalisation without sacrificing general model capabilities or requiring clean reference data.

c828fdddd42f8ffa:2182.summary: Reasoning over incomplete chemical representations like Markush structures remains a challenge for AI-driven scientific discovery, as variable R-group placeholders require grounding across multiple modalities. d72c3221552b0c56:2526.summary: Quantized large language models deployed on edge devices are highly vulnerable to jailbreak attacks because quantization weakens their alignment safeguards. 1f94155a570b5733:2520.summary: The proliferation of AI-generated academic papers has introduced scientific slop, where individual sections look plausible but the global scientific reasoning breaks down. Conventional token-based detectors fail to catch these flaws, but researchers have constructed SciSlopBench using 390 AI-generated papers to benchmark structural and argumentative failures. 22c0e4941496884e:2742.summary: As code generation is increasingly delegated to AI systems, oversight bottlenecks reveal a fundamental vocabulary gap between cybernetic actions and epistemic understanding. To address this, the authors propose a governance criterion requiring consequential choices to carry verifiable conditions and introduce a reconstruction test alongside an ORRCF deliberation-recording convention. 142355993db75860:2733.summary: Agentic AI deployments combine language model inference with tool execution, retrieval, and external access, creating complex security-relevant deviations across entire workflows. A-IDS tracks workflow states, authorization, and communications while explicitly separating evidence capture from operational impact. The model treats prompt injection not just as an input anomaly, but as a potential origin for cascading cross-agent process deviations.

4b9162604f2e157c:2143.summary: Cyber attack agents are traditionally trained and evaluated inside isolated simulators, making it difficult to transfer learned policies across environments with different state representations and action spaces. Researchers demonstrate that simulator-to-simulator and simulator-to-real policy transfers can be treated as an alignment problem by separating state alignment from action translation. Evaluating across four cyber platforms including CyberBattleSim and NASim, zero-shot transfer successfully preserved performance and achieved strong behavioral similarity in emulated virtual machines. These findings prove that RL cyber agents can be ported to new environments without full retraining.
4b9162604f2e157c:2143.one_liner: A new framework enables zero-shot policy transfer for reinforcement learning cyber attack agents across different simulation platforms.
4b9162604f2e157c:2143.bottom_line: Cyber attack reinforcement learning agents can successfully transfer learned policies across different simulation platforms without retraining by decoupling state alignment from action translation.

c7c10a69afb84267:2535.summary: As AI agents delegate tasks across concurrent and failure-prone distributed workers, resource limits act as vital authorization boundaries to prevent catastrophic overspending. 469443f9e5466e36:2373.summary: Decentralized agent economies frequently stitch together independent protocols to complete multi-step tasks, creating a risk where each step looks valid yet the overall outcome fails. For example, escrow contracts may release funds upon an authorized approval that lacks actual evidence of task completion. To analyze this, researchers systematize security and economic requirements across the agent task lifecycle into 17 property families and introduce guarantee closure as a task-relative evaluation criterion. Analyzing 12 systems and 840 matched executions, the study exposes frequent communication failures between verification and settlement stages. These findings highlight the architectural repairs needed to preserve end-to-end cryptographic and economic guarantees.

469443f9e5466e36:2373.bottom_line: Decentralized agent systems suffer from critical disconnects between verification and settlement that require rigorous guarantee closure enforcement.

89764eae00994ca8:16358.summary: Microsoft and Hugging Face researchers introduced ThinkingBox, a benchmark designed to evaluate AI agents by grading their terminal backend state and side effects rather than just looking at final responses or tool calls. In a common-set ablation of 121,680 trials across 12 LLM models, researchers found that 79,853 attempts failed executable backend checks, with 67.24% of those failures still terminating cleanly without a reported tool error. Among those failures, executable checks identified wrong field values in 77.61%, unintended extra effects in 43.30%, and missing required effects in 25.36%. The findings demonstrate a massive gap where AI agents can appear successful while leaving incorrect records behind in databases.

29c4859e9f3e8746:2745.summary: Cybercriminals have been combining customized ChatGPT features with ClickFix social engineering attacks to deliver remote access trojan (RAT) malware. Discovered by Huntress, the campaign uses sponsored search results pointing to a fraudulent CustomGPT named Plus 5.6, which displays a fake service availability notice redirecting victims to a malicious domain. This backup domain poses as a Cloudflare CAPTCHA and tricks users into copying and executing a PowerShell or command prompt command on their local machine. The executed command downloads a malicious MSI file that sideloads malicious code via a legitimate, signed Canon application to establish persistence. The deployed RAT grants attackers capabilities to monitor systems, capture audio and video, exfiltrate data, and deliver secondary payloads, resulting in at least 40 infections before OpenAI took down the initial CustomGPT.

341be5d3b722db0a:2991.summary: The growing adoption of coding and personal AI agents increases the risk of runaway resource consumption and massive cloud bills, making default hard budget caps an essential product feature. Unlike soft caps that only send warning emails after financial limits are breached, hard caps automatically shut down or throttle services when a specified spending threshold is reached. While cloud providers historically resisted blocking production workloads with errors, major platforms are beginning to introduce these controls, with Google Cloud launching Spend Caps in July and AWS releasing monthly spend limits in September. The exposed dataset includes Danish civil registration numbers (CPR), full names, home addresses, work contact details, and next of kin information for nearly 40,000 active users and 160,000 former users. DTU warned that attackers could leverage the stolen CPR numbers and personal data to conduct convincing phishing campaigns and identity fraud. 65216355efd0ae6f:3177.summary: CVE-2026-97644 is a privilege escalation vulnerability in the Groundhogg CRM plugin for WordPress affecting versions up to 4.9. d08779ddfe05ff63:3638.summary: A vulnerability in Bouncy Castle for Java (before 1.86) allows an attacker to impersonate another user in Messaging Layer Security (MLS) groups. The flaw exists because the implementation failed to bind X.509 credentials to the LeafNode signature key, allowing an attacker to present a victim's certificate while signing with an unrelated key. An attacker can exploit this to evict the victim, decrypt group messages, and inject messages as the victim. The fix requires TreeKEM.LeafNode to validate that the end-entity certificate's public key matches the signature key.

d08779ddfe05ff63:3638.bottom_line: If you use Bouncy Castle for MLS, you must update to version 1.86 or later to prevent unauthorized group member impersonation.

claims.text: A party could therefore present another party's certificate as its credential while signing the leaf, and the enclosing KeyPackage, with an unrelated key, and be accepted under that other party's identity
claims.support_span: A party could therefore present another party's certificate as its credential while signing the leaf, and the enclosing KeyPackage, with an unrelated key, and be accepted under that other party's identity through KeyPackage.verify() and the Group leaf-validation path.

2db3ad2a2db41860:3924.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java has disclosed a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71888, affecting the streaming CMS AuthenticatedData parser in versions prior to 1.86, along with specific LTS and FIPS releases. The flaw arises because the parser verifies message content against a MAC based solely on the presence of the digestAlgorithm field, without correctly validating the presence of authAttrs. Consequently, if a message has digestAlgorithm absent but contains attacker-inserted authenticated attributes (such as an RFC 2634 ESSSecurityLabel), the parser verifies the content MAC but returns the unauthenticated attributes as valid. An attacker who can modify a message in transit can exploit this to inject arbitrary attributes that applications rely on for authorization or routing decisions, while the underlying content remains MAC-bound. Bouncy Castle has updated its parsing logic to reject mismatched field pairings.

2db3ad2a2db41860:3924.bottom_line: Applications relying on Bouncy Castle's CMS AuthenticatedData parser can be tricked by transit-modified messages into accepting attacker-inserted security attributes.

2c7dd83ce83ed649:3715.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java versions prior to 1.86 contain a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71889, in both copies of PKIXCertPathReviewer where X.509 name constraints are not correctly applied to the target (end-entity) certificate. Due to a loop bound error starting checks at an index greater than zero, the permitted and excluded subtree checks required by RFC 5280 never ran against the leaf certificate's subject DN or subjectAltName. As a result, certification paths with leaf certificates violating name constraints imposed by their issuing CA were incorrectly reported as valid with empty error lists. Applications relying on the reviewer for trust decisions would consequently accept certificates that the constrained CA was never authorized to issue. Bouncy Castle has updated both reviewer implementations to check every certificate in the path including the target leaf.

712b526d6826a3d3:5839.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java versions before 1.86 harbor a vulnerability, CVE-2026-85515, involving improper handling of OpenPGP message truncation that bypasses SEIPDv1 and AEAD integrity checks. On the SEIPD version 1 path, truncated messages were improperly treated as clean ends of streams without throwing errors, causing PGPEncryptedData.verify() to never execute and delivering CFB-decrypted plaintext without any integrity checks. On the AEAD path, reading in increments smaller than a chunk caused look-aheads to miss trailing authentication tags, silently dropping packets following the literal data. Consequently, truncated messages could be read back as well-formed unsigned or altered plaintexts with no exception raised. Bouncy Castle has updated AEAD decryption streams and close methods to properly throw IO exceptions on truncation.

claims.support_span: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, a truncated OpenPGP encrypted message was accepted with no error reported, and on the SEIPD version 1 path with no integrity check performed at all.

e348483c0fe94c81:3467.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java LTS versions before 2.73.13 contain a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71883, in native packet ciphers for AES-CBC, CCM, CFB, CTR, GCM, and GCM-SIV. The flaw occurs because JNI ReleaseByteArrayElements was invoked in mode 0, which commits native input arrays back to Java arrays even when read-only. When applications encrypted in place—such as passing the same array for both input and destination over `KeyParameter.getKey()`—the subsequent mode-0 release overwrote the newly generated ciphertext with the raw AES key bytes. Consequently, applications received the raw cryptographic key instead of encrypted output without any API indication, leading to keys being transmitted or stored. Bouncy Castle resolved the issue by releasing read-only input arrays with JNI_ABORT.

6552074b98246071:3922.summary: Bouncy Castle for Java versions prior to 1.86 contain a vulnerability, CVE-2026-71890, in the validation logic for Message Layer Security (MLS) external commits (`Group.validateExternalCachedProposals`). While the implementation counted proposal types and bounded removed leaf indices, it failed to verify that the removed leaf was actually owned or associated with the joining participant. According to RFC 9420, external joiners can legitimately remove an old version of themselves during a resync commit, but the lack of credential checks allowed any holder of a group's public `GroupInfo` to commit a Remove proposal naming any member's `LeafIndex`. This forced all group members to evict the targeted participant and allowed the attacker to hijack their slot in the ratchet tree. Bouncy Castle now ensures external commits carrying Remove proposals are accepted only when the removed leaf's credential matches the joiner's new leaf.
6552074b98246071:3922.one_liner: Bouncy Castle MLS implementation flaw allows external participants to arbitrarily remove any group member.
6552074b98246071:3922.bottom_line: Attackers holding a public group info can exploit Bouncy Castle's MLS validation flaw to evict arbitrary group members and hijack their ratchet tree slots.

claims.text: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, validation of an MLS (RFC 9420) external commit's proposal list, org.bouncycastle.mls.protocol.Group.validateExternalCachedProposals, counted the proposals by type and bounded the removed leaf index but never established that the removed leaf had anything to do with the joiner.
claims.support_span: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, validation of an MLS (RFC 9420) external commit's proposal list, org.bouncycastle.mls.protocol.Group.validateExternalCachedProposals, counted the proposals by type and bounded the removed leaf index but never established that the removed leaf had anything to do with the joiner.

claims.text: Any party holding the group's public GroupInfo, which is precisely what an external joiner is meant to be given, could therefore commit a Remove naming any member's LeafIndex and have every member apply it, evicting that member and taking over their slot in the ratchet tree.
claims.support_span: Any party holding the group's public GroupInfo, which is precisely what an external joiner is meant to be given, could therefore commit a Remove naming any member's LeafIndex and have every member apply it, evicting that member and taking over their slot in the ratchet tree.

key_facts: CVE-2026-71890: MLS external commit arbitrary member removal
Affected versions: Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86

a4d6b91fe2106155:1611.summary: A security researcher disclosed a use-after-free vulnerability, designated CVE-2026-20687, in the AppleJPEGDriver kernel component affecting iOS and macOS devices. Tested on iOS 26.3 on an iPhone 17 Pro Max with an A19 Pro chip, the flaw is triggered when an asynchronous decoder timeout causes a request to be freed from a pool without being dequeued from its per-codec vector. A subsequent queue walk dereferences the stale node pointer, leading to a memory tag check fault and an inevitable deferred kernel panic when the Camera app is opened. The researcher released a proof-of-concept application demonstrating the vulnerability execution path.

066dc466bc8ee068:2363.summary: Persona Guardrail is a new production-grade framework designed to secure agentic AI systems by enforcing explicit functional boundaries through semantic allowlists and blocklists. 65abb08e8f25e236:2708.summary: MIRROR is a new communication-layer integrity primitive designed to protect LLM multi-agent systems from Agent-in-the-Middle (AiTM) attacks. By replicating payloads across multiple logical routes and requiring a majority consensus on the message digest, MIRROR ensures integrity without relying on expensive semantic validation or transport-layer encryption. The framework guarantees integrity as long as the number of compromised routes remains below 50%. Testing shows that MIRROR effectively reduces attack success rates to 0% in various topologies while maintaining lower overhead than LLM-as-a-judge approaches.

65abb08e8f25e236:2708.bottom_line: Multi-agent systems require communication-layer integrity primitives like MIRROR to prevent message tampering that bypasses standard transport security.

c5ac943b1560519e:2682.summary: Researchers have identified that security benchmarks for LLM agents are highly sensitive to the representation of threats, a phenomenon they call Threat-Preserving Representation Sensitivity (TPRS). By changing tool names or wording without altering the underlying task or security policy, benchmark scores can fluctuate significantly, leading to unreliable robustness claims. 1add426d5f0a1a33:2663.summary: Researchers introduced the Analytical Memory Unit (AMU), a derivation-gated framework designed for privacy-preserving column-level access control in enterprise AI agent memory stores. Traditional agent memory systems gate retrieval by simple content, ownership, or role, which allows sensitive data leaks through derived computations or permits departments to silently compute conflicting KPIs. The AMU attaches a full lineage graph to every cached result and enforces a retrieval policy that serves a hit only when the requester is authorized for every column touched. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that lineage-gated retrieval removes 18.8% to 25.5% cross-department leakage while preserving over 81% of memory reuse at minimal overhead.
1add426d5f0a1a33:2663.one_liner: Enterprise AI agent developers can use the Analytical Memory Unit framework to prevent sensitive data leakage in shared memory stores via derivation-gated lineage tracking.
1add426d5f0a1a33:2663.bottom_line: Derivation-gated memory frameworks successfully eliminate cross-department data leakage in shared enterprise AI agent memory stores without sacrificing reuse efficiency.

576036d2ff5c6907:2343.summary: Researchers evaluated the assumption that runtime error rates multiply when stacking deterministic rules and LLM judges for agent tool calls across 1,119 labeled actions from three corpora. c4fc110c290e06d7:2678.summary: Researchers introduced Semantic Behavioral Watermarking (SBW) to provide paraphrase-robust and forgery-resistant provenance for LLM agents without modifying output tokens. Traditional agent watermarks bind directly to exact action symbols, causing desynchronization during tool renaming or observation paraphrasing, and fail to prevent adversaries from forging validation trajectories. SBW uses semantic action clusters under history conditioning combined with keyed collision-resistant binning to ensure predictable fresh-bucket assignment in the random-oracle model. Evaluations across five agent models and multiple benchmarks demonstrate high detection robustness under rewriting and superior resistance against adaptive forgeries compared to exact-symbol methods.

1a4f769fda220611:3083.summary: Tuskira has released AI Agent Gateway, an open-source tool designed to sit between AI coding agents and external services to prevent credential leaks. Typically, developers store sensitive model keys and Model Context Protocol (MCP) credentials directly in local agent configurations, exposing them if files are compromised. The gateway intercepts agent requests, validates gateway keys tied to tenant roles, checks tool authorization profiles, and dynamically appends real credentials from an encrypted store right before dispatch. 2c7d30901578d187:2100.summary: LLM-powered AI agents can perform complex tasks but may introduce security risks through unauthorized actions. 78bc6cd5a8f36a44:1630.summary: In Bouncy Castle for Java before 1.86, the Messaging Layer Security implementation failed to properly bind X.509 credentials to a LeafNode's signature_key. Because the implementation stored the certificate chain without validating it or requiring the end-entity certificate's public key to match the signature key per RFC 9420, an attacker could present another party's certificate as its credential while signing with an unrelated key. This flaw allowed an unauthenticated attacker in certain deployments to be admitted under a victim's identity, evict the victim, decrypt group messages, and impersonate them. TreeKEM.LeafNode now strictly requires the end-entity certificate's subject public key to equal signature_key for X.509 credentials, rejecting non-matching leaves.

8b39ddebf5a81afe:2782.summary: Long-term memory agents often retrieve information that is inadmissible for current requests due to policy violations, ownership boundaries, or incompatible lifecycle states. Researchers introduce a retrieval-admissibility verification framework that classifies memory queries, tracks memory IDs, and separates candidate support, admissibility, and prompt exposure evaluation. Evaluations across public benchmarks like RHELM and MemOps show that namespace routing and admissibility filtering significantly improve top-anchor recall and reduce unnecessary similarity evaluations without increasing risk of unauthorized disclosure.

8b39ddebf5a81afe:2782.bottom_line: Separate verification of memory retrieval admissibility from standard relevance scoring to prevent unauthorized context disclosure in LLM agents.

claims.text: We introduce a retrieval-admissibility verification framework that assigns each memory-query pair one of three statuses (admissible, inadmissible, or unresolved), compares routes at matched required-evidence recall with bounds for unresolved cases, and tracks memory IDs through prompt exposure while linking exposure to target-level disclosure.
claims.support_span: We introduce a retrieval-admissibility verification framework that assigns each memory-query pair one of three statuses (admissible, inadmissible, or unresolved), compares routes at matched required-evidence recall with bounds for unresolved cases, and tracks memory IDs through prompt exposure while linking exposure to target-level disclosure.

18ea97ae3381976e:2262.summary: A high-severity vulnerability designated CVE-2026-71886 has been found in Bouncy Castle for Java before version 1.86, affecting the high-level OpenPGP certificate API. The API improperly accepted third-party certifications or trust delegations from component keys of an issuing certificate without verifying whether those components held the CERTIFY_OTHER key flag. As a result, a restricted subkey bound only with SIGN_DATA or an encryption subkey could be promoted to issue positive User ID certifications or direct-key delegations, allowing an attacker to impersonate the offline primary key. The flaw has been addressed by ensuring third-party certifications are only attributed to primary keys or subkeys holding the proper certification key flag.

18ea97ae3381976e:2262.bottom_line: Bouncy Castle versions before 1.86 contain a certificate validation flaw allowing restricted subkeys to act as primary keys in OpenPGP trust delegations.

d9324ea8e07bd1bf:2697.summary: Developers managing fleets of parallel coding agents on single workstations frequently encounter resource starvation and out-of-memory issues because traditional tools like tmux only manage windows rather than memory. To solve this, researchers developed MemMux, a local runtime that implements runtime verification for agent-hosting substrates by providing per-agent attribution, complete process tree reclamation, and escaped-process visibility. Benchmarking shows MemMux successfully keeps an agent fleet under a binding memory budget with zero swap, whereas ungoverned tools push the machine to its RAM ceiling and spill into swap.
d9324ea8e07bd1bf:2697.one_liner: MemMux introduces local runtime verification and resource attribution for fleets of coding agents, preventing out-of-memory crashes and resource leakage.
d9324ea8e07bd1bf:2697.bottom_line: MemMux provides runtime resource governance and memory attribution for parallel coding agents to prevent system instability and unmanaged resource consumption.

claims.support_span: We present MemMux, a local runtime that turns resource governance into checkable signals (per-agent attribution, complete reclamation, escaped-process visibility, bounded footprint under overcommit, and monitoring overhead), with a claims-disciplined benchmark against tmux, a purpose-built agent multiplexer, and a raw-process baseline on identical workloads.

claims.text: Under a binding memory budget on a Linux host, MemMux keeps the fleet under budget (7.5 GiB) with zero swap by admitting a subset and reclaiming under pressure
claims.support_span: Under a binding memory budget on a Linux host, MemMux keeps the fleet under budget (7.5 GiB) with zero swap by admitting a subset and reclaiming under pressure, while the ungoverned tools run every agent, pin the machine at its RAM ceiling (2x over budget), and spill about 2 GiB into swap.

ad1a904649ed37c5:2616.summary: When deciding whether to escalate a query from a small language model to a larger one, semantic entropy can serve as a cheap signal to predict whether escalation will improve accuracy. Evaluated across three benchmarks and two model families, semantic entropy successfully distinguishes small model errors on tasks like GSM8K and improves routed accuracy over random escalation. However, researchers discovered that naive metrics can be easily fooled: a question-only difficulty rule without any model involved matched semantic entropy's performance on a synthetic benchmark. The study outlines critical evaluation checks—such as scoring baseline question-only difficulty, accounting for different definitions of success, and calculating live sampling costs—to ensure escalation signals provide genuine value.
ad1a904649ed37c5:2616.one_liner: Semantic entropy can optimize LLM routing decisions, but robust controls are required to ensure signals outperform basic question-difficulty baselines.
ad1a904649ed37c5:2616.bottom_line: Rigorous baseline controls are necessary when evaluating LLM routing signals like semantic entropy to ensure they genuinely add predictive value over simple question difficulty.

claims.text: On GSM8K, with a small/large pair about twelve times apart in size, semantic entropy reliably distinguishes the small model's mistakes (AUROC 0.871) and improves routed accuracy over random escalation by up to nine points at matched cost.
claims.support_span: On GSM8K, with a small/large pair about twelve times apart in size, semantic entropy reliably distinguishes the small model's mistakes (AUROC 0.871) and improves routed accuracy over random escalation by up to nine points at matched cost.

507c0281250696e6:11359.summary: Integrating Large Language Models into enterprise workflows significantly expands the traditional application security attack surface beyond the model itself. Because LLMs can autonomously invoke tools, retrieve data across APIs, and act as intelligence layers, prompt injections and security flaws can trigger cascading failures across the entire software stack. Conventional security scans and model safety checks often miss these complex attack chains, which can lead to remote code execution, credential theft, and cross-tenant data exposure when service accounts possess overly broad permissions. Security leaders must map what AI systems can access and execute realistic attack scenarios across all underlying infrastructure layers.

507c0281250696e6:11359.bottom_line: Enterprise AI security requires mapping full stack integrations and testing realistic attack chains rather than relying solely on traditional perimeter defenses or model safety scans.

114f9a5ebff393ff:2162.summary: While agentic harnesses can improve Text-to-Image diffusion models via memory, workflow orchestration, and prompt refinement, these performance gains remain external and vanish when the harness is removed. Researchers propose Diffusion On-Policy Context Distillation (D-OPCD), which internalizes the knowledge encoded in the agent harness directly into the weights of the diffusion model. Equipped with an Auto Skill Evolver (ASE), D-OPCD successfully raises average direct-generation scores across four benchmarks and enables continual co-evolution where both the harness and model weights iteratively improve each other.
114f9a5ebff393ff:2162.one_liner: Diffusion On-Policy Context Distillation internalizes agentic prompt-engineering skills directly into diffusion model weights.
114f9a5ebff393ff:2162.bottom_line: D-OPCD distills agentic enhancements into diffusion model weights, allowing generators to retain improved performance without requiring an external harness.

claims.text: We propose Diffusion On-Policy Context Distillation (D-OPCD), which treats the agent-improved prompt as privileged context and distills the knowledge encoded in the agent harness into the weights of the diffusion model
claims.support_span: We propose Diffusion On-Policy Context Distillation (D-OPCD), which treats the agent-improved prompt as privileged context and distills the knowledge encoded in the agent harness into the weights of the diffusion model, so that the model retains part of the harness's benefit when conditioned on the original query alone.

claims.text: Using a Text-to-Image agent equipped with our proposed Auto Skill Evolver (ASE), we show that D-OPCD can internalize harness capabilities into the generator's weights, raising the average direct-generation score from 60.52 to 65.09 across four benchmarks.

64e6aed615c5a2fc:2673.summary: While Large Language Model agents perform well in interactive environments, their ability to continually learn from experience is limited by task-specific memory and the high cost of fine-tuning. aedad04b28ee898f:2764.summary: Researchers have introduced LADE, a model-agnostic defense framework for LLMs that detects and blocks jailbreak attacks using latent safety signals extracted from dark knowledge in the first-token probability distribution. Existing decoding-stage defenses often introduce a utility trade-off or rely on internal hidden states tied to specific architectures. LADE avoids these limitations by contrasting harmful and benign queries via a k-Nearest Neighbors search over mapped safety-discriminative tokens. Experiments show that LADE effectively lowers attack success rates across diverse models while preserving helpfulness on benign inputs.
aedad04b28ee898f:2764.one_liner: A new model-agnostic defense, LADE, uses first-token probability distributions to block LLM jailbreaks without architectural constraints.
aedad04b28ee898f:2764.bottom_line: LADE provides robust, architecture-independent defense against LLM jailbreaks without degrading model helpfulness on benign queries.

claims.text: LADE leverages latent safety signals extracted by contrasting harmful and benign queries from dark knowledge in the first-token output probability distribution.
claims.support_span: To address these limitations, we introduce LADE (Latent Safety Signals for Defense), which leverages latent safety signals extracted by contrasting harmful and benign queries from dark knowledge (i.e., information carried by the output probability distribution beyond its argmax) in the first-token output probability distribution.

e0b81e433e63dafe:2706.summary: Researchers demonstrate that multi-round agreement in medical LLM consensus systems is a fragile proxy for correctness, as models can be unanimously wrong when sharing a foundational misconception. To address this, they developed ProbeGuard, a certified abstention framework that evaluates how consensus is formed rather than just looking at the final output state. ProbeGuard examines process features like agreement trajectories, minority persistence, and rationale semantic entropy while actively probing for counter-evidence. On medical QA benchmarks, the framework significantly raises the discrimination of correct versus incorrect consensus and bounds selective risk.

4bdab949b9c29330:2380.summary: Researchers introduced Supervised Safe-Role Fine-Tuning (SSRFT), a novel safety alignment framework that reformulates LLM safety as the internalization of a predefined safe role rather than relying on explicit refusal patterns. 01a2c6999f99425f:1620.summary: Researchers introduced RAG-PIBench, a leakage-aware benchmark designed to evaluate prompt-injection detection in Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. Containing 4,876 contextual examples split across frozen train, validation, and protected-test sets, the benchmark was built using a leakage-aware pipeline and strict evaluation protocols. The authors compared keyword-based, semantic-reference, TF-IDF, and transformer-based detectors, finding that DistilBERT achieved the best protected-test performance with an F1 score of 0.896 and a PR-AUC of 0.968, while TF-IDF SVM and logistic regression remained strong sparse baselines. These results highlight the importance of leakage-aware benchmark design for reliable prompt-injection security defenses in RAG architectures.

b712d48725a8e262:2362.summary: Persistent agent memory systems often suffer from reliability issues because weak assertions are stored and later treated as established facts. Researchers study whether retention decisions should use a category-conditioned confidence threshold rather than a single global bar, keeping well-evidenced categories while abstaining on unreliable inferences. An empirical evaluation across 4,715 candidate assertions revealed a reliability asymmetry where only 77.9% of value and belief assertions are source-supported compared to 96.2% for other categories. Implementing a stricter category-conditioned threshold on values reduced unsupported retentions from 6.2% to 4.0% while preserving estimation coverage. This approach demonstrates that reliable memory retention depends on semantic category and can serve as effective selective prediction at the write boundary.
b712d48725a8e262:2362.one_liner: Category-conditioned retention thresholds improve LLM agent memory reliability by filtering out unsupported value and belief assertions.
b712d48725a8e262:2362.bottom_line: Using semantic category-conditioned thresholds instead of a global confidence bar significantly reduces unsupported memory retentions in LLM agents.

f133c9e6c99c740d:13862.summary: The 0day Rubbish Research Team disclosed a critical unauthenticated vulnerability in Advantech WebAccess Node 9.2.3, a closed-source industrial SCADA/HMI web server. Tracked with a CVSS score of 9.8, the flaw combines unrestricted file upload (CWE-434), path traversal (CWE-22), and missing authorization (CWE-306) within the CrystalRpt.aspx form handler. An attacker can supply a crafted nodeName parameter with double dot-traversal sequences (	extbackslash..	extbackslash..) to bypass validation checks and write an arbitrary ASP.NET file to the application root directory. Subsequent requests to the uploaded file cause the build manager to compile and execute it within w3wp.exe under high privileges, achieving unauthenticated remote code execution. Mitigation requires proper extension validation and reordering file processing checks before saving files to disk.
f133c9e6c99c740d:13862.one_liner: A critical 9.8 CVSS unauthenticated file upload and path traversal vulnerability in Advantech WebAccess Node allows remote code execution.

bdc134cd22fd6b4e:2387.summary: Prefill-decode disaggregation improves Large Language Model serving efficiency, but static worker ratios frequently cause latency Service Level Objective (SLO) violations during transient and sustained workload shifts. Researchers present FluidPD, a serving system that delivers SLO-aware in-place elasticity for disaggregated P/D architectures without provisioning additional workers or restarting engines. FluidToken addresses transient workload imbalances by offloading a bounded portion of prefill computations to decode workers when decode-side slack is available. Meanwhile, FluidRole handles sustained shifts by dynamically reassigning running workers between prefill and decode roles in place. Guided by lightweight pressure indices, FluidPD improves overall SLO attainment by up to 94.6 percentage points compared to static SGLang configurations across Azure trace workloads.

874d5210faee2d67:2269.summary: Mathematical problem-solving agents frequently delegate deterministic steps to tools that can fail silently. Researchers studied this risk using a controlled framework where a hidden interceptor replaces tool outputs with plausible incorrect data across 31 problems. Results show that without verification, accuracy drops from 100% to 72.4%. Mandatory same-context reflection fully restores accuracy to 100%, whereas optional verification relies entirely on the model choosing to invoke it. Furthermore, full problem restarts succeed 100% of the time following explicit error detection.
874d5210faee2d67:2269.one_liner: Mandatory reflection restores mathematical agent reliability under corrupted tool feedback, whereas optional verification remains inconsistent.
874d5210faee2d67:2269.bottom_line: AI agent architectures must enforce mandatory verification policies rather than relying on optional prompts to maintain reliability against corrupted tool outputs.

376e2aa41da76ed2:2196.summary: Researchers introduced ASAP, an assembly-source aligned pseudocode refinement framework designed to improve binary decompilation using large language models. Traditional decompiler pseudocode is a lossy abstraction for aggressively optimized binaries, so ASAP learns source-aligned assembly representations via joint function-level and snippet-level contrastive alignment. A Q-Former compresses assembly features into tokens that condition the decompilation LLM alongside rule-based pseudocode. Across multiple compiler optimization levels, ASAP improved the average re-execution rate from 64.7% to 71.9% and recompilation rate from 91.6% to 96.6% over strong baselines.

24af79052e6e9716:2315.summary: Internal features in large language models are frequently interpreted as causal mechanisms when tracking concepts, but steering can push features outside their natural operating ranges. The researchers propose an empirical contract involving installation, removal, and downstream rescue tests to evaluate feature behavior at values observed on natural inputs. Testing across representations shows that published unknown-entity latents transfer only a small fraction of the natural abstention contrast when installed. Furthermore, dense known-yellow directions demonstrate opposite asymmetries between installation and removal in Gemma and Llama models. Consequently, tracking a concept and steering a behavior do not inherently prove that a model actively uses that feature during normal computation.
24af79052e6e9716:2315.one_liner: LLM steering experiments do not prove a model relies on a feature unless tested at natural input values.
24af79052e6e9716:2315.bottom_line: Steering a model behavior does not demonstrate that the model naturally utilizes the corresponding internal feature.
